summary: Double routing observed when pin reconciliation race coincides with canary health flapping
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that during a zero-downtime promote for model gptx-2.1-32k, a subset of requests were routed twice (edge -> primary shard AND edge -> fallback shard) resulting in duplicate responses and elevated tail latency. The incident appears tied to a pin reconciliation race where the in-memory tenant pin state was being updated concurrently with canary health probes flipping a host from unhealthy->healthy rapidly due to flapping.

Impact: Affects a single dedicated tenant (ClearFrame Media) during peak traffic windows. Symptoms: duplicated responses for some requests, spikes of 5xx and increased 95/99 latency, and a handful of customer-side application errors due to idempotency violations. Estimated impacted requests: ~0.6% of inbound for the tenant during a 12:00-12:12 UTC window.

Why we care: duplicates and unexpected fallbacks break guaranteed semantics for customers who rely on version pinning for A/B and rollout consistency. This is customer-facing P1 incident for a dedicated customer on a revenue contract.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure tenant-level version pin to model v2 (gptx-2.1-32k) and enable weighted canary set with health checks enabled.
2) Initiate a promote operation that adjusts weights from 100% v1 -> 100% v2 using gradual weight shifts (canary increments).
3) Simultaneously introduce synthetic probe flapping on a canary host (toggle health probe pass/fail every 2s).
4) Send high-concurrency requests that expect a pinned model response and observe routing paths and response duplication.
logs:
2024-10-22T12:01:03Z EDGE router: received request tenant=clearframe session=abc123 route=pin(v2) -> routing-reconciler lookup
2024-10-22T12:01:03Z RECONCILER: pin_lookup returned v2 primary=shard-42 fallback=shard-9 (cache hit ttl=1s)
2024-10-22T12:01:03Z EDGE: forwarded to shard-42 (conn id 785)
2024-10-22T12:01:04Z HEALTH: probe shard-42 failed (latency spike) mark=unhealthy
2024-10-22T12:01:05Z RECONCILER: cache eviction for tenant clearframe triggered; reconciling pins
2024-10-22T12:01:05Z EDGE: fallback routing engaged -> forwarded to shard-9 (conn id 792)
2024-10-22T12:01:05Z RESPONSE: two responses produced for session=abc123 (200 from shard-42, 200 from shard-9) -> duplicate observed by customer
Relevant traces: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/trace-8f72e
Error samples: 5xx rate increased from 0.2% -> 3.4% during window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: race between cache eviction + reconcilier refresh and health probe state change allowed router to concurrently forward the same request to both primary and fallback paths.
Confirmed via trace: two distinct forwards for same request id, forwarded within 200ms of each other. Edge router did not detect dedupe because session affinity token mutated during reconciliation.
Reconciler logs show an aggressive TTL (1s) on pin state update for this tenant due to a prior emergency tweak; this reduced the window for atomic swaps and exposed race.
Health probe flapping amplified the effect: host transiently toggled unhealthy then healthy, causing route recalculation mid-request.
No evidence of model-serving backend duplication; both shards returned legitimate 200s. The problem is at routing/edge-level concurrency semantics.
comments: Diego Alvarez (Support) 2024-10-22: Customer opened ticket; attached request IDs and sample payloads. Customer notes: 'We saw duplicate messages and our idempotency keys failed.'
Maya Chen (SRE) 2024-10-22: Captured traces and linked to observability. Initial mitigation: bumped pin cache TTL to 30s for tenant clearframe to reduce reconciliation churn.

Jorge Martinez (Edge) 2024-10-23: Edge change deployed (hotfix) to serialize per-session routing decisions when a pin update is in-flight. Rolling to us-east. Monitoring shows dup rate falling to baseline.
Customer (ClearFrame) 2024-10-23: Confirmed duplicates stopped after mitigation, asks for root cause and timeline for full fix.
Maya Chen (SRE) 2024-10-24: Flagging follow-ups for product: adjust default pin cache TTLs and improve reconciler atomicity. Will schedule postmortem.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: temporarily increased tenant pin cache TTL to 30s and rolled out edge hotfix to serialize routing decisions during pin-reconcile events. This reduced duplicate responses to near-zero for the tenant. Full fix planned: change reconciler to apply pin state updates using compare-and-swap with a short grace window to drain in-flight requests, and make health-probe flapping detection more conservative (remove <2s toggles as valid state changes).
resolution_notes:
Actions completed:
- Hotfix deployed to edge-router (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/2045)
- Pin cache TTL increased for affected tenant
- Customer confirmed fix
Follow-ups:
- Engineering: implement reconciler CAS and grace-window (owner: @maya) due 2024-11-05
- Product: review default pin TTL settings and add safe-guard for dedicated-tier (owner: @liam)
- SRE: add alert for >0.5% duplicate-response rate per-tenant (owner: @jorge)
Postmortem: scheduled 2024-10-30 in #incidents and Confluence notes page created.
